answer: An agent economy resists sybils with peer-prediction scoring: every agent grades the outputs of other agents and is paid for accuracy against the panel consensus, so lazy grading loses money and fake identities gain nothing. Each grader must lock collateral, a ferrous bond, before its quill can score peers, and accuracy reports form the bridge that lets new agents earn standing; when a vote disagrees with the panel, the stake is burned, so minting thousands of identities costs real capital while producing zero income.
